mn_jeff_s_world_mn_ca_border.blurb: A cluster of granite walls around Crane Lake in far northern Minnesota, in lake country close to Voyageurs National Park, the Boundary Waters and Quetico. Most of the walls are reached by water, so the climbing is spread over several separate crags rather than one cliff. Sport routes make up most of it, with a smaller amount of trad, top-rope and bouldering. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, weighted toward 5.10 to 5.12. Expect slabs, overhangs and roofs; lichen covers some faces, though most lines are clean. Secret Lake, M&M Hill and Swamp Wall are among the larger sub-areas, and some of the surrounding lakes also offer deep-water soloing.

oh_mrg_southwest_aka_western_wetlands.blurb: The south side of Mad River Gorge, in the nature preserve near Springfield in southwest Ohio, where many large trees keep the area well shaded. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with a smaller number of sport routes and only a few trad lines. Boulder problems run from V0 up to around V7, weighted toward the easier and middle grades, while the roped routes mostly fall between about 5.8 and 5.11. Rusty Ravine is a boulder-only sub-area; Ship Rock, Teapot Wall and the Trash Shoot Area hold roped climbs. The preserve as a whole is described as limestone.

tn_prentice_cooper.blurb: Prentice Cooper State Forest lies in the Tennessee River Gorge near Chattanooga. Bouldering dominates the climbing here, with a smaller amount of trad and very little sport. Boulder problems span V0 to V11 with the bulk in the V4 to V8 range, and the few roped routes run from about 5.7 to 5.13. Pot Point, inside the forest, is a bouldering area with hundreds of problems on solid sandstone across a wide range of grades, with views of the Tennessee River. The Tennessee Wall, also in the forest, is hard sandstone with mostly single-pitch trad. Suck Creek Bouldering, T Wall Bouldering and Upper Pot Point are the larger sub-areas.

ut_crawdad_canyon_veyo.blurb: A basalt sport-climbing canyon near Veyo, about 20 miles from St. George in southwest Utah. Dark basalt walls rise to around 80 feet in a wooded canyon, with a creek running through and cottonwoods shading the floor. Every route is a bolted sport climb, mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a fair number of moderates between 5.6 and 5.9. The routes are spread over many separate walls and buttresses, including Flytrap, The Rubicon, Baby Rubicon and Cartoon Crag.

ut_house_range.blurb: A long north-south range in Millard County, in west-central Utah's West Desert, made mostly of gray carbonate rock with a pink granitoid intrusion in its central part. Sport routes outnumber trad here, with most grades between 5.10 and 5.11, some moderates from 5.6 up, and a few 5.12s. The climbing is in canyons and on peaks: Marjum Canyon and West Sawtooth Canyon hold routes, Miller Canyon is another canyon area, and Notch Peak, among the tallest limestone cliffs anywhere, carries long multi-pitch trad lines.

wv_lower_meadow.blurb: The downstream cliffline of the Meadow River Gorge, in the New River Gorge region of West Virginia, on the north side of the river. Five walls make up the area: Tan Wall, Toxic Hueco Area, Greatest Show Area, Moon Wall and Sunkist Wall. Trad and sport are both here, trad a little ahead, with a few boulder problems below. Grades concentrate between 5.10 and 5.12, with a spread of easier climbs from 5.5 and some 5.13s. The gorge's cliffs are sandstone, highly featured with edges, pockets, huecos and jugs. The area gets somewhat more sun than shade and can be climbed year-round.
